# MyRecon

> MyRecon is a public-source OSINT and digital footprint toolkit for auditing
> your own online exposure and conducting authorized research. The web toolkit
> offers username searches, email exposure checks, domain/DNS/IP lookups,
> password leak checks and paid Deep Search. A separate Android app performs
> checks from the handset and is currently in closed testing.

## Product and access

- [Web toolkit](https://www.myrecon.xyz/): Standard username sweeps cover a supported catalogue of 500+ platforms. Guest previews and account/plan limits apply; use the live interface for current access. A matching handle is a lead, not proof that profiles belong to the same person.
- [Email lookup](https://www.myrecon.xyz/#tool=email): Free for guests and signed-in users, with all returned results visible and no paid-plan requirement. Email lookups do not consume username scan allowances. Optional linked-account checks require opting in; unavailable sources remain inconclusive.
- [Features](https://www.myrecon.xyz/features): Current capabilities and public-source limits.
- [Pricing](https://www.myrecon.xyz/pricing): Current free allowances, paid features, supported currencies and Extended scan credits. Read the product page for current prices and terms.
- [Deep Search](https://www.myrecon.xyz/deep-search.html): Paid public-source research by handle or name, including public comments, indexed mentions, owner-declared links and candidate public records. Source availability varies; matches do not confirm identity and an empty response does not prove absence.
- [Android app](https://www.myrecon.xyz/app.html): On-device username checks, breach watch, password leak checks and QR/link safety. Android 11 or newer. Currently in Google Play closed testing; only eligible testers can access the listing until public release.
- [Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.Myrecon.osint): Official Android package com.Myrecon.osint; closed-testing eligibility applies.
- [Footprint removal service](https://www.myrecon.xyz/services.html): A separate paid, human-run service. Read its scope and terms before requesting assistance.

## Evidence and interpretation

Username results distinguish found, not_found and unknown. HTTP 200 alone is
not account proof. Blocks, rate limits, login walls and ambiguous responses
can remain unknown. Review source evidence before acting, and do not equate a
missing result with a clean footprint. Coverage counts describe supported
platforms, not a guarantee that every source responds successfully.

- [Username benchmarks](https://www.myrecon.xyz/#benchmarks): Measurements, methodology, unknown outcomes and raw evidence. The daily benchmark covers GitHub, GitLab and Hacker News; it does not establish accuracy across the entire platform catalogue.
- [Why username checkers report fake accounts](https://www.myrecon.xyz/guides/why-username-checkers-report-fake-accounts.html): Control-handle methodology and the limits of HTTP status checks.
- [What HTTP responses reveal](https://www.myrecon.xyz/guides/what-http-responses-reveal.html): Soft 404s, login walls and ambiguous responses.
- [Verify an OSINT finding](https://www.myrecon.xyz/guides/verify-an-osint-finding.html): Corroboration and identity-matching limits.
- [Is MyRecon legit?](https://www.myrecon.xyz/is-myrecon-legit.html): Checks readers can perform themselves and limitations to consider.
- [Tool comparisons](https://www.myrecon.xyz/vs/): Named comparisons with methodology and tradeoffs. Read the current page and evidence before making a comparative claim.
- [Username Sweep vs Deep Search](https://www.myrecon.xyz/username-sweep-vs-deep-search.html): Differences between direct platform checks and broader public-source research.

These articles answer questions about public-source tools, social media OSINT,
reverse username searches and digital footprint checks. Tool lists are the
publisher's editorial selections, with product limits and source links;
list positions are not independent rankings or endorsements.

## Public breach metadata API

- [Developer documentation](https://www.myrecon.xyz/developers.html): Public versioned JSON endpoints, examples, attribution and licensing requirements.
- [API discovery](https://www.myrecon.xyz/data/v1/index.json): Endpoint directory.
- [Breach metadata](https://www.myrecon.xyz/data/v1/breaches.json): Public breach descriptions; this dataset cannot be queried for a person's email address.
- [Latest breaches](https://www.myrecon.xyz/data/v1/latest.json): Latest entries in the public metadata feed.

Have I Been Pwned is the source of its licensed breach metadata; MyRecon is
the distributor. Credit the original source as required by CC BY 4.0 and the
developer documentation. Do not describe metadata as leaked passwords or
personal breach records.

## Limits and policies

MyRecon does not grant access to private profiles or bypass login walls.
Public name matches and matching usernames require independent verification.
It does not provide face recognition or guaranteed phone-number-to-person
identification. Use is limited to self-audits and authorized research under
the terms; harassment, stalking and doxxing are prohibited.

- [Privacy policy](https://www.myrecon.xyz/privacy.html): Current storage, providers and data-handling details. Do not describe the service as zero-logging.
- [Terms](https://www.myrecon.xyz/terms.html): Authorized use and service limits.
- [About](https://www.myrecon.xyz/about.html): Product background.
- [Founder](https://www.myrecon.xyz/founder.html): Maintainer background.
- [Contact](https://www.myrecon.xyz/contact.html): Support and inquiries.
- [Sitemap](https://www.myrecon.xyz/sitemap.xml): Public indexable pages.
